structure.title: Preface
structure.summary: This letter from ICICI Bank to stock exchanges announces the 31st Annual General Meeting (AGM) on August 30, 2025, via video conferencing. It encloses the AGM Notice, Annual Report 2024-25, and Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report, available on the bank's website. The documents are sent electronically to registered members, with web-link/QR code letters for others and physical copies upon request. An annexure details the AGM business: adoption of financial statements, dividend declaration, re-appointment of a director, reappointment of two joint statutory auditors, appointment of a secretarial auditor, and revisions in remuneration for the MD & CEO and Executive Director. Copies are sent to NYSE, Singapore Stock Exchange, Japan Securities Dealers Association, and SIX Swiss Exchange.

structure.title: Ordinary Business Resolutions for Thirty-First AGM
structure.summary: The annexure lists ordinary business resolutions to be transacted at the Thirty-First AGM through remote e-voting and e-voting during the AGM. Resolutions include adoption of audited standalone and consolidated financial statements for FY ended March 31, 2025; declaration of dividend on equity shares for the year ended March 31, 2025; re-appointment of Mr. Sandeep Batra as a Director retiring by rotation; re-appointment of M/s. B S R & Co. LLP as Joint Statutory Auditors from the conclusion of the Thirty-First AGM to the Thirty-Third AGM; and re-appointment of M/s. C N K & Associates LLP as Joint Statutory Auditors for the same period.

All items are categorized as ordinary business.

key_items: INSTRUCTIONS ON DEDUCTION OF TAX AT SOURCE ON DIVIDEND

It also specifies requirements for non-resident shareholders, covering ADR depositary, FIIs/FPIs, and others, including tax treaty benefits with necessary documents like PAN, TRC, Form 10F, and self-declarations. The Bank reserves the right to request further information and apply domestic law or tax treaty provisions.

It covers tax rate application for multiple accounts under a single PAN, Rule 37BA provisions for tax deduction in the name of another person, reliance on details as of the record date (August 12, 2025), and the deadline for submitting documents to determine the appropriate tax rate. It explains dividend payment after TDS, dispatch of TDS certificates, no communication after the deadline, refund options, indemnification for misrepresentation, and that the communication is not tax advice. It also mentions reliance on Income Tax website verification for higher TDS under Section 139AA.

structure.title: NOTES
structure.summary: This annual report excerpt commemorates ICICI's 70-year journey, from its founding in 1955 as India's first private development financial institution to its evolution into a leading private bank. It outlines key milestones, including the 1994 launch of ICICI Bank, the 2002 merger, and pioneering technological innovations like internet banking, ATMs, and mobile apps. A detailed timeline highlights significant contributions to industrial finance, venture capitalism, insurance, and digital services for retail and MSME customers. The text also reflects on the institution's legacy of building trust, driving inclusive growth, and its continued focus on innovation and lasting value creation.

structure.title: The Evolution of a Legacy:

It also outlines the Annual Report 2025, prepared per Indian regulations and the International Integrated Reporting Framework, providing a comprehensive view of operations, performance, strategy, governance, risks, and six capitals. Reporting boundary focuses on ICICI Bank Limited, with the period April 1, 2024 to March 31, 2025. A safe harbour statement addresses forward-looking statements and risks. The contents list integrated and statutory reports, financial statements, and additional disclosures like Basel Pillar 3 and glossary.

structure.title: MESSAGE FROM THE CHAIRMAN
structure.summary: This Chairman's message introduces Pradeep Kumar Sinha as the new Chairman, acknowledging his predecessor. It reviews India's resilient economy and ICICI Bank's healthy Fiscal 2025 performance, including improved profitability, a resilient balance sheet, and stable capital. The Bank focuses on risk-calibrated growth via ecosystems, micromarkets, and quality counterparties, aiming for 'Return of Capital' and a stable funding profile. Customer-centricity is emphasized through 'Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank' and 'One Bank, One Team,' leveraging data analytics and digital infrastructure, with investments in cybersecurity. ESG progress includes a carbon neutrality target by fiscal 2032 and climate risk management. CSR initiatives, primarily via ICICI Foundation, focus on healthcare, environment, livelihoods, and community development, including a cancer care facility. The Board ensures strong governance, compliance, and integrity. The message highlights India's long-term potential and ICICI's 70-year legacy, expressing commitment to sustainable value creation.

It emphasizes the 'One Bank, One Team' culture, operational resilience, risk management, compliance, and sustainability toward carbon neutrality. CSR efforts via ICICI Foundation benefited 19 million people. It discusses enhancing customer relationships, launching DigiEase for business banking onboarding, efficient resource use, and investments in technology, AI, and iCRM for better customer experience and operational effectiveness.

structure.title: OUR BUSINESS STRATEGY
structure.summary: The section outlines the Bank's business strategy for sustainable outcomes through disciplined execution. It highlights 70 years of service, strong financial performance (profit before tax up 11.4% to ₹607.13 billion, domestic loans up 13.9%, deposits up 14.0%), and a vision to be the trusted financial service provider. The strategy rests on three pillars: Principles (Return of Capital, Fair to Customer and Bank, One Bank One Team, Agile Risk Management, Compliance with Conscience); Coverage (Customer-360º, micromarkets, ecosystems, partnerships, and digital/physical network); and Delivery Framework (quality focus, process decongestion, and BankTech leveraging APIs, cloud, AI/ML). It emphasizes integrity, transparency, fairness, and operational resilience to create stakeholder value.

nodes.title: OUR BUSINESS STRATEGY (intro)
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's business strategy, emphasizing disciplined execution focused on capital, counterparty, and capacity for sustainable outcomes. It highlights 70 years of service, strategic pillars of principles, coverage, and delivery framework, and core principles like Return of Capital, Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank, One Bank One Team, and Compliance with Conscience. It details financial performance: profit before tax excluding treasury grew 11.4% to ₹607.13 billion, domestic loans grew 13.9% to ₹13,109.81 billion, and deposits grew 14.0% to ₹16,103.48 billion. The strategy includes granular loan growth, resilient balance sheet, right counterparties, capital preservation, agile structures, and delivery framework. It lists approach elements: principles, coverage (micromarkets, customer 360°, collaborations, ecosystems), and delivery framework (maximizing profit before tax, quality, process decongestion, Bank to BankTech, simplify). The vision is to be the trusted financial service provider, investing in operational resilience and delivery channels for secure, stable banking, with integrity, transparency, and fairness to create sustainable stakeholder value.

nodes.title: I. PRINCIPLES
key_items: a. Return of Capital; b. Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank; c. One Bank, One Team; d. Agile Risk Management
b. Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's guiding principles for building stakeholder trust and a risk-compliance culture. It details five principles: (a) Return of Capital, prioritizing capital conservation through prudent risk management, granular lending, and right counterparty selection; (b) Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank, emphasizing fair value, transparency, and customer-centric initiatives like removing prepayment charges; (c) One Bank, One Team, focusing on unified customer service, organizational realignment, employee skills, and 'seva bhaav'; (d) Agile Risk Management, advocating dynamic, data-driven, forward-looking risk identification and mitigation; and (e) Compliance with Conscience, committing to legal and ethical business practices, supported by a Risk and Compliance Culture Policy and employee workshops.

nodes.title: II. COVERAGE
nodes.summary: The section outlines ICICI Bank's coverage strategy centered on Customer-360º, micromarkets, ecosystems, and partnerships. It emphasizes a holistic customer approach, transforming branches into business centres, restructuring teams, and empowering frontline staff. The micromarket focus leverages data analytics for localized strategies and tailored propositions, supported by V-Serv Plus and organizational strengthening. The ecosystem strategy captures entire value chains with sector-specific solutions across physical and digital channels. Collaborations include cross-functional teams, technology partnerships, co-branded cards, FASTag expansion, and startup engagement, adopting AI, ML, and cloud computing for innovation and efficiency. As of March 31, 2025, the network comprises 6,983 business centres, 16,285 ATMs/cash recycling machines, and 1,058 digital service kiosks.

nodes.title: a. Focus on Customer-360º
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's customer-centric coverage strategy, emphasizing a holistic approach to serving banking needs across ecosystems and micromarkets. It details the Customer-360º focus, including understanding customer needs, transforming branches into business centres, restructuring teams for leadership presence, and empowering frontline staff. It highlights leveraging business centres, digital channels, partnerships, and overseas coverage for growth, with corporate office serving as a service centre. It also provides ICICI Bank's network figures as of March 31, 2025: 6,983 business centres, 16,285 ATMs/cash recycling machines, and 1,058 digital service kiosks.

nodes.title: b. Focus on Micromarkets
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's micromarket-focused strategy, using data analytics and market intelligence to empower frontline teams with localized strategies and tailored propositions. It highlights V-Serv Plus for expert-guided customer query resolution, and the empowerment of frontline teams with detailed local insights for personalized experiences. Organizational strengthening includes State and City Business Heads and Credit Business Centres for faster processing. The combination of micromarket insights and digitisation drives growth and efficiency, with the network comprising 6,983 business centres as of March 31, 2025. The strategy also covers focus on high-potential markets, leadership presence, asset distribution, business centre expansion, risk-calibrated profitability, and leveraging high-potential segments and ecosystems.

nodes.title: c. Focus on Ecosystems
nodes.summary: The Bank aims to serve customers' ecosystems by capturing the entire value chain, including channel partners, dealers, vendors, and employees, through a full-bank approach. It develops sector-specific solutions addressing industry nuances to support businesses throughout their journey, delivered via physical and digital channels. Services include cash management, cross-border/domestic trade, and supply chain finance for customers and employees, catering to sectors like broking, custodian services, real estate, education, FMCG, healthcare, NBFC, pharmaceutical, and retail. The strategy emphasizes enhancing ecosystem opportunities, identifying value chain opportunities, 360-degree solutions, execution focus, and covering stakeholders such as MNCs, corporates, capital markets, merchants, GCC, healthcare, NRIs, golden years, defence, students, and housing societies. The Bank is digitally transforming cross-border trade to streamline journeys, simplify transactions, enhance value creation, and build a resilient, technology-powered ecosystem for seamless, secure experiences, enabling cross-selling and holistic solutions on scalable, secure, regulatory-aligned infrastructure.

nodes.title: d. Collaborations and Partnerships
nodes.summary: The text covers collaborations and partnerships as a key focus area, including cross-functional teams for ecosystem coverage, partnerships with technology companies for growth and customer experience, and 360° solutions for new-to-bank customers via co-branded credit cards with digital onboarding. It highlights FASTag usage expansion to parking payments, and collaboration with startups through a platform for co-creating innovative solutions aligned with the digital roadmap. Startup partnerships aim to unlock opportunities, strengthen risk frameworks, enhance customer experience, and drive operational efficiency. The Bank uses a structured engagement framework and adopts technologies like AI, ML, computer vision, and cloud computing across retail, NRI, corporate banking, treasury, customer service, risk, compliance, and legal operations, delivering impacts such as video KYC, supply chain financing, AI/ML Bank Guarantee processing, speech recognition, collateral management, and satellite data for collection efficiency and rural underwriting.

nodes.title: III. DELIVERY FRAMEWORK
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's Delivery Framework, focusing on enhancing customer experience through simplified banking. It covers three key areas: Focus on Quality, emphasizing stringent counterparty selection and data analytics for quality onboarding; Process Decongestion, detailing efforts to eliminate complexity, streamline operations, and improve turnaround times via technology, digital public infrastructure, and initiatives like One KYC and 3-in-1 accounts, plus organizational changes like OpsServe and V-Serv; and Leveraging BankTech, describing progress in technology platforms, embedded banking, cloud adoption, data analytics, AI, and an enterprise architecture framework with over 5,500 APIs, all guided by scalability, resilience, and security principles. The framework aims to build a seamless, sustainable delivery system across technology, operations, policies, structure, and distribution channels.

structure.title: Technology Architecture and Focus Areas
structure.summary: The section on Technology Architecture and Focus Areas outlines the Bank's business strategy, emphasizing a technology architecture with focus areas on engagement (decongested, personalized experience), federation (microservices, secured interface), data & intelligence (real-time, AI adoption), and core platforms (modular architecture, lightening the core). It highlights investments in observability platforms, an integrated zero-trust security architecture, and operational resilience. AI adoption spans credit risk, marketing, fraud detection, document extraction, and image recognition. Generative AI and digital platforms are detailed, including AI investments, cautious use cases, and digital transformation through mobile banking, internet banking, UPI, digital wallets, self-service devices, and various digital solutions like iMobile, iLens, InstaBIZ, and API Banking. The iMobile One App Strategy focuses on a seamless, secure, personalized banking experience with over 400 services, iFinance for personal finance management, enhanced features like UPI for NRIs, smart scan, voice search, security features like iMobile SmartLock, and streamlined Video-KYC and re-KYC processes.

The page also lists app sections such as Spends, Borrow, Travel/Shopping/Offers, Scan to Pay, Payments, Smart Lock, Deposits & iFinance, and Loans/Cards.

structure.title: All-new icicibank.com - A New Era of Simple Banking
structure.summary: The text outlines ICICI Bank's business strategy for an all-new icicibank.com, emphasizing simple, fast, fresh, transparent, and personalised banking. It describes the website redesign, which offers a seamless, user-friendly, and personalised experience with features like simplified product discovery, easy comparisons, interactive calculators, and save-for-later options. The website now serves as a business enablement platform with digital journeys for customers and non-customers, and redesign of remaining sections continues. Additionally, it mentions iCRM and the 'One Bank, One Team' principle, noting a transformation during fiscal 2025.

structure.title: Unified CRM Platform
structure.summary: The text describes a unified CRM platform integrated with core banking systems, offering simplified customer onboarding, relationship enrichment, holistic enhanced relationship management, Customer-360° coverage, automated service and escalation framework, intelligent insights, service fulfilment, real-time nudges and updates, streamlined omni-channel communication, centralized customer engagement memory, and accelerating data intelligence. It details the iCRM platform as a cross-functional unified platform connecting users, data, and key customer information across the Bank, designed for web and mobile with real-time insights, powered by cloud-based enterprise solution, serving about 100 thousand users across 7,000 business centres, integrating over 50 internal systems, and providing omni-channel experience. It also introduces iLens, an integrated digital lending platform for retail loans covering the entire loan life cycle, initially for mortgages and expanded to personal and education loans.

structure.title: iLens: One Digital System for all Retail Lending Products
key_items: InstaBIZ: All-in-One App for Business Banking
structure.summary: The text describes ICICI Bank's iLens digital platform for retail lending products (mortgage, personal, education loans, credit cards), covering onboarding, verification, decisioning, and disbursal workflows for all stakeholders. It highlights seamless paperless journeys, automated verification, API integration, risk management, instant sanctions, digital disbursements, KYC, flexible application modes, cloud-native architecture, and the TrackMyApplication interface. It also introduces InstaBIZ, an all-in-one business banking app launched in 2019, offering loans, overdrafts, trade management, payments, analytics insights, and SmartLock for channel security, emphasizing continuous improvement for customer experience. The text also mentions credit cards introduced in fiscal 2025 to enhance Customer-360° value.

structure.title: InstaBIZ: Business Banking App
structure.summary: The section covers ICICI Bank's digital banking initiatives and business segments. It details InstaBIZ, a business banking app, and DigiEase, a digital onboarding platform launched in fiscal 2025 that integrates GST, MCA, bank statements, and ITR for seamless data retrieval, real-time checks, and end-to-end visibility. It outlines the First Time Right business strategy and digital platforms for corporate customers, including cash management, trade solutions, cross-border payments, liquidity management, and specialized services like Digi-Escrow, Trade Online, Trade API Suite, Insta EPC, e-Docs, e-LC, and e-BL. It also covers digital solutions for NRIs and summarizes business segments: NRI banking, retail and rural banking, business banking, wholesale banking, international business, and government banking, along with digital platforms, risk management, and customer experience enhancements.

nodes.title: InstaBIZ: Business Banking App (intro)
nodes.summary: The text covers InstaBIZ, a business banking app, and DigiEase, a digital onboarding platform launched in fiscal 2025 that integrates with GST, MCA, bank statements, and ITR for seamless data retrieval, real-time checks, and end-to-end visibility from onboarding to portfolio monitoring, ensuring first-time-right efficiency. It also details digital platforms for corporate customers, including cash management, trade solutions, cross-border payments, liquidity management, and specialized services like Digi-Escrow, Trade Online, Trade API Suite, Instant EPC, e-Docs, e-LC, and e-BL, emphasizing integrated, intuitive solutions for businesses.

nodes.title: DigiEase Digital Onboarding Platform and Business Strategy
key_items: DigiEase: End-to-End Digital Onboarding Platform for Business Banking Customers
nodes.summary: The page outlines the business strategy using a First Time Right approach with data integration, efficient resource use, real-time tracking, and a fully digital onboarding journey. It introduces DigiEase, launched in fiscal 2025, as an end-to-end digital onboarding platform for business banking customers. DigiEase integrates with public data infrastructure like GST, MCA, bank statements, and ITR to enable seamless digital data retrieval and validation, ensuring reliability and eliminating manual verification. It provides real-time checks on decision-making parameters, regulatory compliance, and operational efficiency with reduced turnaround time and cost. The platform offers complete visibility across onboarding, sanctioning, disbursement, and portfolio monitoring, ensuring timely updates and a frictionless journey. By consolidating multiple digital services into a single workflow, DigiEase enhances productivity and accuracy through a first-time-right approach.

nodes.title: Digital Platforms and Solutions for Corporate Customers
nodes.summary: The Bank provides innovative digital platforms for large corporates, focusing on integrated, seamless solutions. It enhances cash management and trade platforms for domestic and cross-border payments, liquidity, and treasury management. The Digi-Escrow platform digitizes escrow services. Cross-border solutions include Trade Online, Trade API Suite, Insta EPC, digital document management (e-Docs, i-Docs, e-Softex, i-BOE), and digital FX/trade services (e-LC, e-BL, integrated FX). Supply chain finance platforms like OneSCF, FSCM, CorpConnect, and DigitalLite offer partner onboarding, dealer/vendor financing, visibility, reconciliation, dashboards, and smart credit assessments using GST data, bureau checks, and AI. The trade API suite, using multithreading, digitizes trade transactions for speed, security, compliance, efficiency, and transparency.

nodes.title: Digital Solutions for Non-Resident Indians
nodes.summary: The text covers ICICI Bank's business segments: NRI banking with simplified digital onboarding, re-KYC, and cross-border remittances; retail and rural banking with 8.9% and 5.1% advances growth, digital initiatives, and analytics-driven underwriting; business banking with 33.7% growth, DigiEase platform, and program-based lending; wholesale banking with 14.3% growth, relationship-led strategy, and supply chain financing; international business with overseas offices, GIFT City IBU offerings, and four strategic pillars; and government banking with digital solutions, fund flow mechanisms, and tax collection services. The text also details digital platforms, risk management, and customer experience enhancements across segments.

structure.title: f/)/CICI Bank
structure.summary: The text outlines ICICI Bank's commitment to a risk and compliance culture, emphasizing balanced risk-reward and fair, transparent dealings. It details fiscal 2022's Risk and Compliance Culture Policy, which sets guiding principles and requires a governance framework defining roles for the Board, MD & CEO, Executive Directors, and Risk and Compliance Culture Council, plus continuous communication and business compliance officers. It references the ICICI Group Code of Business Conduct and Ethics guiding employee decisions and stakeholder commitment. Five guiding principles are listed: One Bank, One Team; Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank; Return of Capital is Paramount; Compliance with Conscience; and Agile Risk Management.

structure.title: OUR VALUES
structure.summary: The text outlines ICICI Group's values, including its Code of Business Conduct and Ethics and key policies covering conflict of interest, confidentiality, anti-bribery, personal investment, record accuracy, KYC/AML/CFT, asset protection, workplace responsibilities, and social media. It details a zero-tolerance approach to bribery and a Board-approved KYC/AML/CFT policy with risk-based measures, suspicious transaction monitoring, name screening, sanctions lists, and cross-border screening. It also covers the Group Compliance Policy's framework emphasizing regulatory adherence and fairness, continuous review of financial controls, and governance practices, plus periodic employee training and awareness e-mailers on fraud risk, data privacy, cybersecurity, compliance, conflict of interest, and sexual harassment.

structure.title: FAIR TO CUSTOMER, FAIR TO BANK
structure.summary:

The Bank continues to build seamless customer journeys, focus on process reimagination and further strengthen delivery through digital platforms to enhance customer delight, efficiency and resilience.
In fiscal 2025, the Bank continued to focus on making customer journeys frictionless and delivering customer delight by placing the customer at the centre of every design and process reimagination. We are harnessing new-age technologies and platforms to enable us to serve our customers with simplicity.

structure.title: FAIRTOCUSTOMER,FAIRT
key_items: Hotline; RM Callback; Voice BOT 2.0; Systemic Callback Functionality
Upskilling Voice RMs to Handle Multiple Products
structure.summary: ICICI Bank's customer-centric approach uses continuous listening and learning from feedback, complaints, NPS, and root cause analysis to improve services. Key voice channel enhancements include Virtual Hold, V-Serv, Voice Biometric verification (3.36 million calls in FY25), WhatsApp digital adoption, AI-driven Digital Email Manager, RM enablers like Hotline and callbacks, Voice BOT 2.0, systemic callback for dropped calls, and multi-product RM upskilling. New digital experiences feature revamped iMobile and RIB interfaces, address updates via Aadhaar OTP, QR login, simplified Re-KYC, and nominee updation. Employee service enablers include Branch On the Move, expanded loan and demat servicing, and monthly capability forums. NPS improved, reflecting customer value creation.

structure.title: CUSTOMER SERVICE AND GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL
structure.summary: The text details the Bank's customer service and grievance redressal framework, including Board and standing committee oversight. It covers compliance with the Customer Rights Policy (fair treatment, transparency, suitability, privacy, grievance redress) and efforts for customer education and needs-based product offerings. Complaints are handled through multiple channels, recorded in a CRM system with an escalation matrix and turnaround times, and analyzed via root cause analysis for process improvement. Internal Ombudsmen and various committees monitor service at different levels, emphasizing responsiveness, learning from complaints, and continuous improvement to strengthen customer relationships.

structure.title: CUSTOMER ENGAGEMENT BEYOND BANKING
structure.summary: The text describes a bank's monthly e-magazine, The Orange Book, launched to simplify personal finance and improve financial literacy. It covers basic topics like compounding and emergency funds, and advanced themes such as goal-based investing, tax-saving, succession planning, nominations, and will writing. Using examples, infographics, games, and puzzles, it also educates customers on emerging financial frauds. The initiative builds financial confidence and has been well-received. The text includes annual report references, volume and date details, and taglines like 'Fair to Customer, Fair to Bank' and 'Rewind, Look Forward.'

structure.title: DATA PROTECTION AND PRIVACY
structure.summary: The Bank is committed to data privacy compliance across its global jurisdictions, including India and overseas offices. It employs a centralised strategy with defined principles for handling customer data, a personal data incident reporting mechanism, and a Personal Data Incident Handling Forum (PDIHF) for investigation and monthly reporting. The Bank's Personal Data Protection Standards ensure data security through technical and organisational measures like access control, encryption, impact assessments, and training. It categorises personal data as Confidential Information, records processing activities, signs confidentiality agreements, and offers customers rights. Employee awareness is built via e-learning, periodic trainings, mailers, and initiatives. A governance framework includes the Data Protection Officer, Privacy Steering Committee, and Code of Business Conduct guidelines.

structure.title: RISK GOVERNANCE FRAMEWORK
structure.summary: The Bank's Risk Governance Framework emphasizes responsible growth through effective governance, risk culture, and enterprise risk management, covering credit, market, liquidity, operational, technology, cyber, third-party, compliance, legal, and reputation risks. The Board oversees risks via specific committees (Credit, Audit, IT Strategy, Risk), mostly chaired by Independent Directors, with defined mandates. Independent groups—Risk Management (Credit, Market, Operational, Financial Crime), Compliance, Internal Audit, and Information Security—monitor risks. Key frameworks include ERM, Risk Appetite, Stress Testing, and ICAAP. The Chief Data Officer leads data governance. Cybersecurity governance involves multi-level oversight, policies aligned with global/domestic standards, 24x7 SOC, DLP, and ISO 27001 certification. IT governance includes Board sub-committees and steering committees.

structure.title: Controls for IT Infrastructure
structure.summary: The text outlines the Risk Governance Framework's IT infrastructure controls, categorized as preventive (e.g., ASLC, VAPT, access management), detective (e.g., SOC monitoring, RED teaming), and responsive (e.g., incident response plans, forensic agreements). It details participation in external cyberattack simulations like spear phishing, DDoS drills, and social engineering tests, plus BCP/DR drills validated against RTOs. It describes the CSIRT and IRP for incident response, customer data protection and awareness campaigns, and notes no material security breaches in fiscal 2025. Finally, it covers ESG progress, including data management, disclosure alignment, and Board/Risk Committee reviews.

structure.title: ESG RATINGS
structure.summary: The text covers the Bank's ESG ratings and governance. External agencies Sustainalytics and MSCI evaluate ESG practices; Sustainalytics score improved from 22.5 (Medium Risk) to 18.9 (Low Risk) in fiscal 2025, while MSCI rating remained A. SEBI-approved Indian ESG rating providers also publish scores based on BRSR and public disclosures, ranging from 69 to 76 out of 100. ESG governance structure includes the Board of Directors (annual update), Risk Committee (semi-annual reporting), ESG Steering Committee (quarterly meetings), and a dedicated team in the CFO's office tracking ESG and CSR initiatives. An overarching Environmental, Social and Governance Policy covers responsible financing, environmental sensitivity in operations, customers, employees, society, corporate governance, cybersecurity and data privacy governance framework, and stakeholder engagement and accountability, and is available on the Bank's website.

structure.title: ESG-related Developments during Fiscal 2025
structure.summary: The text covers the Bank's risk governance framework and ESG developments in fiscal 2025. ESG initiatives include a digital tool for data management, progress toward carbon neutrality with I-RECs, increased emissions due to heatwaves and expansion, water generators, paper reduction, occupational health and safety improvements, climate risk identification, and stakeholder engagement. Risk management covers traditional risks (economic, credit, market, liquidity, operational) and emerging climate risks, with a Climate Risk Management Framework and participation in policymaking. Specific responses to economic, credit, and market/liquidity risks are detailed, including monitoring, stress testing, and policy reviews.

structure.title: RESPONDING TO RISKS AND OPPORTUNITIES
structure.summary: The report covers two sections. First, it outlines five key risk types—operational, cyber, technology, employee, and compliance—detailing each risk and the Bank's response, including risk management policies, cyber defenses, technology investment, employee development, and compliance culture. Second, it describes the materiality assessment process for ESG topics, including benchmarking against GRI, SASB, and DJSI, stakeholder engagement via surveys, and a five-step approach that identified 14 topics, with 10 shortlisted as most relevant for long-term growth.

structure.title: MATERIALITY ASSESSMENT
structure.summary: The Bank conducted a materiality assessment to identify and prioritize ESG issues relevant to its business and stakeholders, re-examining topics since the previous assessment in fiscal 2022. The approach included benchmarking against GRI, SASB, and DJSI, and peer benchmarking, followed by shortlisting topics for stakeholder feedback via a survey involving employees, customers, investors, vendors, and industry partners. A five-step approach was adopted: identifying ESG topics, analysis and prioritization, shortlisting, stakeholder engagement, and stakeholder identification. The Bank identified 14 material topics and shortlisted 10 most relevant for sustainable long-term growth, covering environmental, social, and governance aspects such as carbon emissions, corporate governance, customer fairness, employee practices, customer experience, cybersecurity, digital innovation, risk management, leadership development, and financial performance. The text also lists all 14 topics and notes that details are in the ESG report.

structure.title: HUMAN CAPITAL
structure.summary: The text covers ICICI Bank's human capital strategy, emphasizing a culturally aligned workforce with the right attitude, skills, and 'seva bhaav' under the 'One Bank, One Team' philosophy. It details the human capital strategy's pillars: fair compensation, learning and growth, and care, aimed at fostering a customer-centric, innovative, and agile workforce. Organisational design principles focus on customer-centricity, reducing silos, and decentralising decision-making. Fair compensation is guided by the Board and BGRNC, comprising fixed and variable pay, with share-linked instruments for around 20,769 employees. Recruitment strategy includes 'hire for attitude, train for skill', digital tools like iUniverse, industry-academia partnerships, and new programs such as the ICICI Bank Aspire program.

structure.title: LEARNING AND GROWTH
structure.summary: The text covers the Bank's human capital learning and growth initiatives, including over 10 million learning hours in fiscal 2025, averaging 10 learning days per employee, with a capability building architecture for functional training, leadership development, digital skilling, and industry-academia collaborations. It details industry academia partnerships such as the 12-month Probationary Officers Program, 21-day Post Graduate Programme in Relationship Management, 12-month Young Leaders Program, Ascend Programme, and 12-month Business Leadership Program certification in securities markets. The mandatory Customer-360° Program equips relationship managers with product knowledge, digital propositions, compliance, and scenario-based interactions, with advanced modules in trade products, business banking, and asset products. Risk and compliance workshops engaged about 31,000 employees in 2025, integrated into the Branch Leadership Program.

structure.title: ICICI Bank Human Capital Training and Leadership Initiatives
key_items: Job Rotation and Moving Across Roles
structure.summary: The page details ICICI Bank's human capital initiatives: the Business Centre Program trains branch leaders in customer-centric, risk-compliant practices; Functional Academies offer domain-specific training; the Digital Academy supports BankTech skilling in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, and more via PRISM and partnerships; Leadership Development includes regular sessions, investor forums, 'Leading – the ICICI way', the 'Ignite' series, and a Leadership Academy; Learning Assessment uses the Learning Matrix with an 80% pass criterion for feedback; Academic Councils review content alignment; Job Rotation enables cross-functional skill-building; and Succession Planning uses the Senior Management Cover Index to track leadership bench depth.

structure.title: CARE
structure.summary: The text covers the Bank's human capital focus, emphasizing employee care through an inclusive, meritocratic workplace with Officer Like Qualities (OLQ). It details a 24x7 emergency helpline, Quick Response Teams, hospital tie-ups, group insurance, and a Parental Insurance Scheme. It highlights women's empowerment via key positions and policies like maternity, childcare, adoption, fertility leave, Travel Accompaniment, and support for children with special needs. It also outlines the Prevention of Sexual Harassment framework, including awareness via mandatory e-learning and a confidential complaint mechanism, plus iCare for other workplace queries.

structure.title: EMPLOYEE CONNECT AND ENGAGEMENT
structure.summary: The text covers ICICI Bank's employee engagement and human capital initiatives. It details communication channels like Leadership Engagement Sessions, quarterly updates, 'Conversation' sessions, and 'I-Engage' onboarding to foster open dialogue on culture, ethics, compliance, and performance. The iCare platform provides multi-channel employee support with AI chatbot for queries and grievances. The iUniverse digital careers platform streamlines candidate experience from application to onboarding. Universe on the Move (UOTM) is an AI/ML-powered comprehensive employee lifecycle tool integrating HRMS and CRM for services like leave, payslips, lead creation, and approvals, with geo-fencing and security features.

structure.title: Employee Service Platforms: iCare, iUniverse, and Universe on the Move
structure.summary: The page covers ICICI Bank's employee service initiatives: the iCare Service platform for quick resolution of people-process queries, service requests, and grievances via multi-channel support and an AI chatbot; iUniverse, a digital careers platform offering candidates a seamless application-to-onboarding experience with real-time updates and support; and Universe on the Move (UOTM), an API-integrated business tool for the employee lifecycle using AI/ML for customized user experience, integrated with HRMS and Sales CRM, featuring geo-fencing sign-in, investment declarations, lead creation, and approvals. It also highlights HR services anytime, anywhere, including leave application, payslips, seamless business transactions, and one-stop employee services.

structure.title: Learning Matrix
structure.summary: This text from an integrated annual report covers human capital development through the AI-enabled Learning Matrix digital platform, which provides online libraries, social learning, curated open content, AI-driven learning recommendations, and content curation based on feedback for on-the-go employees. It explains access via laptop/desktop and the mobile app path. It lists AI/ML and functional skill courses including iMobile Modules, Data Protection, and Data Science for Practitioners, with 'Start Learning' links, and includes the report's statutory/financial statements structure and Annual Report 2024-25 page number.

structure.title: SOCIAL AND RELATIONSHIP CAPITAL
key_items: Service aspects considered important by our customers:

structure.summary: The Bank emphasizes responsible communication and trustworthy conduct with stakeholders to create sustainable value. It engages key stakeholders: customers through multiple channels and feedback mechanisms to ensure fair treatment and right-selling; shareholders/investors via meetings and disclosures on strategy, governance, and ESG; employees through townhalls, apps, and grievance portals, focusing on inclusive culture, learning, and well-being; society via ICICI Foundation's CSR activities in healthcare, environment, and livelihoods, plus value chain engagement on ESG; and regulators through ongoing communication and compliance. Each section details engagement methods, stakeholder priorities, and the Bank's responses, including policy updates, training, and technology use.

structure.title: CORPORATE SOCIAL RESPONSIBILITY
structure.summary: The text covers ICICI Bank's Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and financial inclusion efforts. It details CSR philosophy, fiscal 2025 spending of ₹8.01 billion via ICICI Foundation, and key thematic areas: healthcare (50 hospitals, 0.4 million impacted, cancer care facilities with Tata Memorial Centre), environment (water conservation, 4.9 million saplings, 56 forest reserves), livelihood (5.2 million impacted), and community development. It highlights the SHG programme impacting 11 million women with 9.8 lakh loans, microfinance outreach to 2.2 million customers, JLG lending, and 4.9 million PMJDY accounts. It also describes Digital Banking Units (DBUs) and their fiscal 2025 performance metrics, including accounts, loans, transactions, and awareness camps.

structure.title: ENVIRONMENT AND SUSTAINABILITY
structure.summary: The text covers the Bank's environment and sustainability initiatives, including its 70-year history and commitment to sustainable growth. It details efforts to measure and mitigate environmental impact through a dedicated team, reducing energy and waste, paper conservation via e-statements, and the 'Go Green' trademark. It discusses building capabilities for carbon footprint measurement and data governance. Sustainable financing is outlined, with a portfolio of ₹906.24 billion across renewable energy, EVs, green real estate, etc., and green financing at 34.2%. The approach to ESG and climate risk in risk management includes an ESG risk assessment tool, sustainable financing framework, and climate risk management framework. The text also covers environmental sensitivity in operations, such as renewable energy procurement, I-RECs, AWG installations, recycled paper use, and nature-based CSR projects.

structure.title: BOARD’S REPORT
structure.summary: The Board's Report covers ICICI Bank's financial highlights, dividend recommendation of ₹11 per share, and appropriations for fiscal 2025. It details share capital allotments, loans and investments disclosures, and subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures, including ICICI Securities' delisting. Changes in directors and key managerial personnel are outlined, along with auditor appointments, secretarial audit, and compliance certificates. The report includes related party transactions, annual return, BRSR, integrated reporting, risk management framework, POSH Act disclosures, and corporate governance practices. It concludes with acknowledgements and compliance confirmations.

nodes.title: ICICI Bank Board Report: Financial Highlights, Dividend, and Appropriations
nodes.summary: The page presents the Board's Report for ICICI Bank's 31st Annual Report for fiscal 2025. It includes Financial Highlights comparing fiscal 2025 and 2024 performance metrics such as net interest income, operating expenses, core operating profit, provisions, profit before tax, treasury gains, tax, profit after tax, and consolidated profit figures. The Dividend section outlines the bank's consistent dividend policy and recommends a dividend of ₹11.00 per equity share for the year ended March 31, 2025. The Appropriations section details the allocation of accumulated profits for fiscal 2024 and 2025, including transfers to statutory reserve, special reserve, capital reserve, investment fluctuation reserve, revenue and other reserves, dividend paid, and balance carried forward, with footnotes explaining the investment fluctuation reserve and dividend payment.

nodes.title: Share Capital Allotments and Loans, Guarantees, Investments Disclosures
key_items: PARTICULARS OF LOANS, GUARANTEES OR INVESTMENTS
nodes.summary: The page covers two sections of a Board's Report. SHARE CAPITAL details equity shares allotted during the year: 42,832,398 shares under the ICICI Bank Employees Stock Option Scheme-2000, 751,672 shares under the ICICI Bank Employees Stock Unit Scheme-2022, and 56,008,117 shares allotted on March 26, 2025, pursuant to a Scheme of Arrangement for delisting ICICI Securities. It references Schedule 1 of the financial statements for details. PARTICULARS OF LOANS, GUARANTEES OR INVESTMENTS states that under Section 186(11) of the Companies Act, 2013, provisions except sub-section (1) do not apply to loans, guarantees, or security provided by a banking company in the ordinary course of business. It notes that particulars of investments are disclosed in Schedule 8 of the financial statements per the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.

nodes.title: SUBSIDIARY, ASSOCIATE AND JOINT VENTURE COMPANIES
nodes.summary: The text details ICICI Bank's subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures as of March 31, 2025, noting ICICI Securities' delisting and conversion to a wholly-owned subsidiary effective March 24, 2025, with no changes in joint ventures during fiscal 2025. It lists 17 subsidiaries (including step-down subsidiaries) and 8 associate companies with their shareholding percentages, and includes footnotes on joint venture classifications, share purchases, and associate statuses. It also summarizes performance highlights, references to consolidated financial statements and Section 129 statement, availability of subsidiary financial statements, confirmation of no significant regulatory orders or material changes affecting financial position, updates on the scheme of arrangement for ICICI Securities' delisting including share allotment, and changes in Board composition and Key Managerial Personnel.

nodes.title: ICICI Bank Board Report: Subsidiaries, Material Changes, and Scheme of Arrangement
key_items: MATERIAL CHANGES AND COMMITMENT AFFECTING FINANCIAL POSITION OF THE BANK
nodes.summary: The text covers ICICI Bank's Board Report, including: share sales in FISERV Merchant Solutions and NIIT Institute of Finance Banking and Insurance Training, both ceasing as associates; highlights of subsidiaries, associates, and joint ventures performance and contribution; availability of separate audited financial statements and consolidated financial statements incorporating subsidiaries; confirmation that no significant material orders by regulators or courts impact going concern status; no material changes affecting financial position post-financial year; and an update on the scheme of arrangement for delisting ICICI Securities, which became a wholly owned subsidiary effective March 24, 2025, with shares allotted to public shareholders on March 26, 2025.

nodes.title: DIRECTORS AND OTHER KEY MANAGERIAL PERSONNEL
nodes.summary: The text details changes in Board composition and Key Managerial Personnel (KMP): appointments of Pradeep Kumar Sinha as Independent Director and Part-time Chairperson, Ajay Kumar Gupta as Executive Director, Rohit Bhasin and Punit Sood as Independent Directors; re-appointments of Rakesh Jha and Sandeep Batra as Executive Directors with RBI approval; retirements of Girish Chandra Chaturvedi, Uday Chitale, and Hari L. Mundra; current KMP list; declaration of independence by Independent Directors; and retirement by rotation of Sandeep Batra.

nodes.title: AUDITORS
nodes.summary: The text covers auditor appointments and compliance: statutory auditors B S R & Co. LLP and C N K & Associates LLP were appointed at the 2024 AGM and proposed for re-appointment from the 31st to 33rd AGM with RBI approval; secretarial auditor Alwyn Jay & Co. was appointed for FY2025, and Parikh Parekh & Associates is proposed for FY2026-2030; no cost records are required; no frauds were reported; employee particulars are in an annexure; internal controls are adequate; and a FEMA compliance certificate was obtained from statutory auditors.

nodes.title: Board's Report: Auditor Appointments, Personnel, Internal Controls, and FEMA Compliance
key_items: DISCLOSURE UNDER FOREIGN EXCHANGE MANAGEMENT ACT, 1999
nodes.summary: The page covers the Board's Report sections: re-appointment of joint statutory auditors (B S R & Co. LLP and C N K & Associates LLP) for a three-year term subject to member and RBI approval, with no audit qualifications; appointment and re-appointment of secretarial auditors (Alwyn Jay & Co. for FY2025 and Parikh Parekh & Associates for FY2026-FY2030) with no adverse remarks; availability of secretarial compliance report; non-applicability of cost record maintenance for banks; no fraud reporting by auditors; personnel disclosures under Section 197(12) with annexure available for inspection; adequacy of internal controls over financial reporting with periodic testing; and FEMA compliance certificate from statutory auditors regarding investments in subsidiaries and associates.

nodes.title: Board Report: Related Party Transactions, Annual Return, BRSR, Integrated Reporting
nodes.summary: The page covers four sections: Related Party Transactions, including the Board-approved Group Arm’s Length Policy, arm’s length compliance, material transaction details in Annexure B, SEBI Listing Regulations filings, AS-18 disclosures in financial statements notes, policy revision to align with December 2024 SEBI amendments, and AGM resolutions; Annual Return in Form MGT-7 to be hosted on the Bank’s website; Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report under SEBI Regulation 34(2)(f) to be hosted online with copy available from the Company Secretary, plus ESG Reports released since fiscal 2020 and the fiscal 2025 report; and Integrated Reporting, covering adoption of the International Integrated Reporting Framework since fiscal 2019 and access to the fiscal 2025 report in the Annual Report 2024-25.

nodes.title: RISK MANAGEMENT FRAMEWORK
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's risk management framework, detailing Board oversight and committee roles: the Risk Committee reviews policies for credit, market, liquidity, operational, model risk, early warning signals, outsourcing, business continuity, risk appetite, ERM, ICAAP, stress testing, limits, Basel migration, and liquidity contingency plans; the Credit Committee handles credit proposals, sector exposures, large borrowers, and portfolio reviews; the Audit Committee oversees internal audit, financial reporting, and regulatory compliance; the ALCO manages liquidity and interest rate risk; and the GRMC oversees group risk. It describes policies as the governing framework, independent risk groups (Risk Management, Compliance, Corporate Legal, Internal Audit, Information Security, Financial Crime Prevention) with the Risk Management Group's subgroups, and the GCRO's reporting lines. The Internal Audit Group provides independent assurance and reports to the Audit Committee.

nodes.title: INFORMATION REQUIRED UNDER THE SEXUAL HARASSMENT OF WOMEN AT WORKPLACE (PREVENTION, PROHIBITION & REDRESSAL) ACT, 2013
nodes.summary: The text states the Bank's policy against sexual harassment and formal complaint process align with the POSH Act, 2013, including compliance with Internal Committee constitution. It reports complaint statistics for the financial year: 117 filed, 117 disposed off, and none pending at year-end, noting complaints received during fiscal 2025 were closed within the 90-day turnaround time.

nodes.title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE
nodes.summary: The CORPORATE GOVERNANCE section details ICICI Bank's governance framework, emphasizing an independent Board, ethics, and compliance. It covers the Group Code of Conduct, Insider Trading Code, material subsidiaries (notably ICICI Prudential Life Insurance), familiarisation programmes, dividend and whistle blower policies, and CEO/CFO certifications. It outlines fund utilisation, auditor fees, credit ratings, and a Company Secretary certificate on director disqualification. It describes the Board's composition, meetings, committees (Audit, Governance, CSR, Credit, Customer Service, Fraud Monitoring, IT Strategy, Risk, Stakeholders Relationship, and others), their terms of reference, composition, and attendance. It includes remuneration policies, performance evaluation, disclosures under Section 197(12), senior management changes, general body meetings (AGMs, postal ballots), disclosures on penalties and related-party transactions, means of communication, shareholder information, listing details, shareholding pattern, and various statutory disclosures.

nodes.title: CORPORATE GOVERNANCE (intro)
nodes.summary: ICICI Bank's corporate governance framework relies on an independent Board, separation of supervisory and executive roles, and Board committees, with Independent Directors chairing most committees as of March 31, 2025. The philosophy emphasizes high governance standards, compliance, accountability, transparency, and ethical conduct. The text covers the Group Code of Business Conduct and Ethics, reviewed annually, and the Code on Prohibition of Insider Trading. It addresses material subsidiaries, noting ICICI Prudential Life Insurance Company Limited as a material listed subsidiary with incorporation details and statutory auditors. It also describes the familiarisation programme for Independent Directors, the Dividend Distribution Policy, and the Whistle Blower Policy, including its reporting mechanism to the Audit Committee and investigation process.

It lists Directors' names, attendance, other directorships, and committee memberships. Committee terms of reference and attendance are referenced but not detailed.

nodes.title: II. Audit Committee
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Audit Committee's Terms of Reference and Composition. It details responsibilities: directing audit function, monitoring internal/statutory audit quality, examining financial statements and auditors' reports, overseeing financial reporting, reviewing quarterly/annual statements and MD&A, recommending auditor appointments/remuneration/removal, approving auditor payments, reviewing auditor independence and audit effectiveness, approving related party transactions and subsidiary investments, reviewing whistle-blower mechanism, internal controls, compliance with audit reports, internal investigations, management letters, share investments and advances, reviewing fund utilization statements, monitoring issue proceeds, discussing audit scope, examining defaults, valuation, risk management, inter-corporate loans, appointing accounting firms, establishing complaint procedures, engaging counsel, funding advisors, overseeing regulatory compliance, commenting on merger schemes, and approving CFO appointment. Composition lists twelve meetings held in 2024-2025 and member attendance details.

nodes.title: III. Board Governance, Remuneration & Nomination Committee
nodes.summary: This section covers the Board Governance, Remuneration & Nomination Committee (BGRNC): its Terms of Reference (director appointments, performance evaluation, remuneration policies, diversity, employee stock schemes) and composition/meeting attendance. It details the Audit Committee's empowerment and the BGRNC's composition and director appointment policy. The remuneration policy outlines three segments (wholetime directors/employees, non-executive directors, part-time chairperson) with specific fees, fixed remuneration, and expense reimbursements. Performance evaluation of the Board, Committees, and Directors is described, including criteria and fiscal 2025 outcomes. Executive Director remuneration tables and perquisites, stock options, and notice periods are provided, along with non-executive director sitting fees. Disclosures under Section 197(12) of the Companies Act, 2013 include remuneration ratios, percentage increases, median employee remuneration, and employee counts. Finally, changes in Senior Management Personnel during fiscal 2025 and the list as of March 31, 2025, are presented.

nodes.title: Terms of Reference

nodes.title: Composition

nodes.title: Remuneration policy
nodes.summary: The text outlines the Bank's Compensation Policy, aligned with RBI circulars and Companies Act 2013. It details three segments: Part A for wholetime Directors and employees per RBI guidelines; Part B for Non-executive Directors (excluding Government Nominee and Part-time Chairperson); and Part C for Non-executive Part-time Chairperson. It specifies remuneration for Non-executive/Independent Directors, governed by the Banking Regulation Act 1949, RBI guidelines, and Companies Act 2013. It includes sitting fees, a fixed annual remuneration of ₹3,000,000 for eligible Non-executive Directors effective February 10, 2024, approved by Members on May 14, 2024, and for the Part-time Chairperson, a fixed remuneration of ₹5,000,000 effective April 1, 2024, plus office, travel, and other expenses. All Non-executive/Independent Directors are entitled to expense reimbursement.

nodes.title: Performance evaluation of the Board, Committees and Directors

It details evaluation methods using questionnaires, criteria for assessing the Board (roles, responsibilities, strategic issues, feedback, information flow), Directors (participation, contribution, guidance), Chairperson (leadership, meeting management, stakeholder interests), and Committees (mandate clarity, terms of reference, deliberation effectiveness). It notes action points from fiscal 2024 were addressed, fiscal 2025 evaluation used an electronic survey and was completed satisfactorily, and specific action points were identified for execution. It references note 52 of Schedule 18 for wholetime Directors' evaluation details.
